CANONICAL_NAME.value: Espresso -- two-level Boolean logic minimizer (UC Berkeley)

VERSION.value: github.com/classabbyamp/espresso-logic master as of 2026-09-12 (a build-fixed mirror of the Berkeley source)

value.lineage: Espresso (1980s, Brayton/Hachtel/McMullen/Sangiovanni-Vincentelli, UC Berkeley): heuristic two-level logic minimisation (EXPAND / REDUCE / IRREDUNDANT over cube covers); the tool that defined PLA minimisation and seeded logic synthesis

HUMAN_PROBLEM.value: two-level Boolean minimisation for hardware synthesis

value.built_to: minimise a two-level Boolean function (a truth table / PLA) to the fewest product terms, so the circuit that implements it is smaller and faster
value.pressure: the exponential number of prime implicants; exact minimisation (Quine-McCluskey) is intractable, so Espresso is a heuristic that gets near-optimal covers fast
value.success_means: a correct, much smaller SOP cover of the same Boolean function, in seconds on functions that defeat exact methods

ANCESTRY.value: Espresso (1980s, Brayton/Hachtel/McMullen/Sangiovanni-Vincentelli, UC Berkeley): heuristic two-level logic minimisation (EXPAND / REDUCE / IRREDUNDANT over cube covers); the tool that defined PLA minimisation and seeded logic synthesis

cut.note: heuristic minimisation of a Boolean cover by iterating three operations on the set of cubes until the cube count stops falling: EXPAND each cube to a prime against a representation of the OFF-set so it covers as many other cubes as possible, IRREDUNDANT drop cubes not needed for the cover (a covering problem on a table), REDUCE shrink each cube to the smallest that still covers its essential points so the next expansion can move; essential primes are removed first and appended at the end; two escape moves (last_gasp, super_gasp) try once more when the loop stalls; a final make_sparse pass; the cost is (cubes, total literals) compared lexicographically

provenance.grade_basis: Techne FOSSIL_PACKET.json PROVENANCE_GRADE where issued, else the record's handoff string mapped (populated per R34; Harmonia may re-grade)

organs.human_name: espresso() (espresso.c 1-70): EXPAND, IRREDUNDANT, essential(&F, &D) removed; do { do { copy_cost; REDUCE; EXPAND; IRREDUNDANT } while (cost.cubes < best_cost.cubes); super_gasp / last_gasp } while (cubes fall or, at equal cubes, total falls); append E; make_sparse
organs.mechanism: after an initial expand and irredundant pass, cubes that no other prime can replace (essential) are set aside so the loop works on the rest; the inner loop reduces, expands and makes irredundant while the cube count decreases; when it stalls, a gasp step (reduce each cube, expand it in a different direction, and keep any that let another cube be dropped) is tried and the outer loop repeats if it helped; the cost compares cube count first and literal count second; the essentials are appended and a sparse-variable clean-up runs
organs.input: a cover F (and don't-cares D, off-set R)
organs.output: a smaller cover of the same function
assumptions: a local minimum of the expand/reduce/irredundant cycle is close to the global one on real PLAs; reduce moves the cover off a plateau by shrinking cubes in a new order each time (the toggle in reduce.c)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: near-minimal two-level logic for PLAs in seconds, when exact minimisation (Quine-McCluskey) was infeasible; the algorithm every logic synthesis tool inherited
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: a heuristic with no optimality bound; order-dependent (use_random_order exists); the literal count is a tie-breaker only
organs.human_prior: Brayton, Hachtel, McMullen, Sangiovanni-Vincentelli 1984 (Logic Minimization Algorithms for VLSI Synthesis); MINI (Hong, Cain, Ostapko 1974) as the ancestor of the expand/reduce idea

organs.human_name: expand (expand.c 30-70 and expand1, not read): mini_sort(F, ascend) or random_order; RAISE / FREESET / INIT_LOWER / SUPER_CUBE / OVEREXPANDED_CUBE; the header: 'we do NOT require an unwrapped version of the OFF-set'
organs.mechanism: cubes are processed in an order that starts from the cover's edges; for each non-prime cube the free parts (those that can be raised without hitting the off-set) are determined against the off-set cover directly; parts are raised preferentially so that the expanded cube covers other cubes of the on-set (which then become redundant); when no cube can be covered, a covering heuristic picks a large prime; the overexpanded cube (all individually raisable parts) and the supercube of coverable cubes bound the choices
assumptions: testing containment against the off-set cover is cheaper than complementing (the Espresso-II improvement over the manuscript); covering other cubes is the right greedy objective
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: primes without enumeration; the step that does the minimisation
organs.source_boundary: expand / expand1; CANDIDATE because expand1 was not read

organs.human_name: reduce (reduce.c header: 'the smallest cube contained in the cube which can replace the cube ... the super cube of all of the essential points'; two orderings alternated by a toggle); irredundant / mark_irredundant (irred.c: relatively essential Rt / partially redundant Rp; an sm_matrix covering table solved by minimum_cover)
organs.mechanism: reduce replaces each cube by the smallest cube that still covers the points no other cube covers (computed directly as a supercube), processing cubes in one of two orders alternately so successive passes explore different directions; irredundant partitions the cover into relatively essential cubes (kept), totally redundant (dropped) and partially redundant cubes, and solves a set-covering problem over the last group with a heuristic minimum-cover routine to keep a minimal subset
assumptions: shrinking cubes toward their essential points frees room for a different expansion (the escape from local minima); minimum cover is NP-hard, so a heuristic is used
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the two steps that turn a greedy expand into an iterative improvement
organs.source_boundary: reduce.c, irred.c; CANDIDATE because bodies were not read

pressures.source_evidence: espresso.c; expand.c; reduce.c; irred.c; the examples directory as the benchmark set
pressures.condition: an organism rewrites a cover of a multi-output Boolean function (with don't-cares) into another cover; the score is cube count, then literal count, against the exact minimum on the standard PLA benchmarks; time is bounded
pressures.resource_or_constraint: polynomial passes over the cover; a covering-table heuristic
pressures.failure_condition: covers far from the exact minimum, or time exponential in inputs
pressures.world_punishes: Quine-McCluskey prime enumeration (exponential); a single greedy expansion (local optimum)
pressures.world_rewards: expand/reduce alternation with order changes, irredundant covering, gasp escapes
pressures.observable_consequence: cube count vs exact (where computable) on the Berkeley PLA set, for expand-only, expand+irredundant, and the full loop with and without gasps; run time vs inputs
pressures.vacuity_condition: functions whose primes are all essential
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: the exact minimiser on small cases (a bound, not a competitor)
pressures.cheat_control: an organism given the exact minimum cover must reproduce it; expand-only must show a larger cover on the benchmarks; the full loop must close most of the gap: the world must show all three
pressures.purpose_separated_from_pressure: PURPOSE: two-level logic minimisation (Brayton et al. 1984)
